cohort: 1724 women who delivered macrosomic newborns (>90th percentile birth weight) from 37 weeks gestation in France over a 10-year period
finding: Maternal height < 160 cm, nulliparity, history of caesarean section, excessive uterine height, induction of labour, and duration of labour > 10 h were significant risk factors for caesarean section in women delivering macrosomic newborns.
mod_finding: The caesarean section and instrumental extraction rates were 24.1% and 15.7%, respectively, among women who delivered macrosomic newborns.
